DECLARE Word : STRING

DECLARE Number : INTEGER
DECLARE Index : INTEGER
DECLARE L1 : CHAR

DECLARE Continue : BOOLEAN
INPUT Number
FOR Index ← 1 TO Number
    INPUT Word
    Continue ← TRUE
    V1 ← 1
    V2 ← LENGTH(Word)
    WHILE Continue = TRUE AND V1 < V2 DO
        L1 ← SUBSTRING(Word, V1, 1)
        L2 ← SUBSTRING(Word, V2, 1)
        IF L1 <> L2
          THEN
            Continue ← FALSE
          ELSE
            V1 ← V1 + 1
            V2 ← V2 - 1
        ENDIF
    ENDWHILE
    IF Continue = TRUE
      THEN
        OUTPUT "Successful"
      ELSE
        OUTPUT "NOT successful"
    ENDIF
NEXT Index

A program is required to allow students to calculate the volume of a number of standard three-dimensional shapes. It will use functions to allow other shapes to be added in the future.
  • Cuboid: volume = base × depth × height
  • Triangular prism: volume = ½ × base × depth × height
  • Sphere: volume = 4/3 × Pi × radius × radius × radius
Pi is a constant with value 3.142
Write a program that meets the following requirements:
  • Output a menu to ask the user for an input to indicate the shape for which a volume needs to be calculated, from the three shapes given or if they want to stop the program. The program must validate the input.
  • Input the data needed to calculate the volume of the chosen shape, based on the given formulae.
  • Create one function for each shape to calculate and return the volume using the given formulae. Each function uses the input data as parameters.
  • Output the volume in the main program, rounded to two decimal places.
The program continues until the user inputs the stop option from the menu.
You must use pseudocode or program code and add comments to explain how your code works.
All variables and constants used must be declared for this algorithm.
All inputs and outputs must contain suitable messages.

R2: inputs the data needed for the chosen shape

g: Marked in levels: AO2 (up to 9 marks) for the programming techniques and data structures used; AO3 (up to 6 marks) for comments, meaningful identifiers, logic and accuracy.

CONSTANT Pi ← 3.142
DECLARE Choice : INTEGER
DECLARE Base, Depth, Height, Radius, Volume : REAL

// one function for each shape
FUNCTION Cuboid(B : REAL, D : REAL, H : REAL) RETURNS REAL
    RETURN B * D * H
ENDFUNCTION
FUNCTION Prism(B : REAL, D : REAL, H : REAL) RETURNS REAL
    RETURN 0.5 * B * D * H
ENDFUNCTION
FUNCTION Sphere(R : REAL) RETURNS REAL
    RETURN 4 / 3 * Pi * R * R * R
ENDFUNCTION

REPEAT
    // show the menu and validate the choice
    REPEAT
        OUTPUT "1 Cuboid, 2 Triangular prism, 3 Sphere, 4 Stop"
        INPUT Choice
    UNTIL Choice >= 1 AND Choice <= 4
    IF Choice = 1 OR Choice = 2
      THEN
        OUTPUT "Enter the base, depth and height"
        INPUT Base
        INPUT Depth
        INPUT Height
        IF Choice = 1
          THEN
            Volume ← Cuboid(Base, Depth, Height)
          ELSE
            Volume ← Prism(Base, Depth, Height)
        ENDIF
        OUTPUT "Volume: ", ROUND(Volume, 2)
    ENDIF
    IF Choice = 3
      THEN
        OUTPUT "Enter the radius"
        INPUT Radius
        OUTPUT "Volume: ", ROUND(Sphere(Radius), 2)
    ENDIF
UNTIL Choice = 4

A collector needs a video library system for a collection of videos stored on 4K Blu-ray discs, standard Blu-ray discs, DVD, or as digital downloads.
The two-dimensional (2D) array Video[] is used to store, for each video item, the title, the format of the video (4K Blu-ray disc, standard Blu-ray disc, DVD, or digital download), the year it was released stored as a string and a storage code to represent where the video can be found in the collection, for example:
  • Video[1,1] is "Macbeth"
  • Video[1,2] is "digital download"
  • Video[1,3] is "2015"
  • Video[1,4] is "DG276"
The two-dimensional (2D) array Results[] is used to store the results of a search to find a specific video. The search uses the video title, and if the video is found, its data is copied from the array Video[] to the array Results[]. The search continues and if other videos with the same title are found, this data is also copied to the array Results[]. The search ends when the end of the data is reached.
Write a program that meets the following requirements:
  • The video library array needs to be initialised with the null string (""), allowing for up to 10 000 records. The array Results[] must be initialised before every search with the null string and must be able to hold up to 20 search results with the same title.
  • Create a menu to add a new video to the library, to search for an existing video by title, or to stop, with validation of the input.
  • When the user enters a new video, the video title, format, year of release (as a string) and storage code are stored in the first available location of the relevant array.
  • Allow input of data for another video if required.
  • When searching for an existing video, if a match is found, transfer all the data for that video into the array Results[], and continue to search until all videos with the same title have been found.
  • Output the results from the array Results[]
  • If the video title is not found, output a suitable message.
  • The system returns to the menu after completing the input or the output, until the user chooses to stop.
You must use pseudocode or program code and add comments to explain how your code works.
You do not need to declare any arrays, variables or constants. You may assume that this has already been done.
All inputs and outputs must contain suitable messages.

R2: enters data and stores it in the first available location; allows more data to be input as required (counting, selection, input, storage, iteration)
R3: finds the title using a linear search, copies matches into Results[] and outputs them, with a message if not found; continues until the user stops (input, output, linear search, iteration)
g: Marked in levels: AO2 (up to 9 marks) for the programming techniques and data structures used; AO3 (up to 6 marks) for comments, meaningful identifiers, logic and accuracy.

All inputs and outputs need suitable messages.
ms.code:
// initialise the Video array
FOR Index1 ← 1 TO 10000
    FOR Index2 ← 1 TO 4
        Video[Index1, Index2] ← ""
    NEXT Index2
NEXT Index1
REPEAT
    // show the menu and validate the choice
    OUTPUT "Enter 1 to add a new video, 2 to search for a title, or 3 to stop"
    REPEAT
        INPUT Answer
        IF Answer <> 1 AND Answer <> 2 AND Answer <> 3
          THEN
            OUTPUT "You must input 1, 2 or 3, please try again"
        ENDIF
    UNTIL Answer = 1 OR Answer = 2 OR Answer = 3
    IF Answer = 1
      THEN
        // find the next free space in the array
        Store ← 1
        WHILE Video[Store, 1] <> "" DO
            Store ← Store + 1
        ENDWHILE
        // enter data until the user says no more
        REPEAT
            OUTPUT "Enter the title"
            INPUT Video[Store, 1]
            OUTPUT "Enter the format"
            INPUT Video[Store, 2]
            OUTPUT "Enter the year of release"
            INPUT Video[Store, 3]
            OUTPUT "Enter the storage code"
            INPUT Video[Store, 4]
            Store ← Store + 1
            OUTPUT "Another video (Y or N)?"
            INPUT Another
        UNTIL Another = 'N' OR Another = 'n'
    ENDIF
    IF Answer = 2
      THEN
        // clear the Results array before every search
        FOR Index1 ← 1 TO 20
            FOR Index2 ← 1 TO 4
                Results[Index1, Index2] ← ""
            NEXT Index2
        NEXT Index1
        OUTPUT "State the title of the video you want"
        INPUT Title
        Search ← 1
        Store ← 1
        // linear search, copying every match into Results
        REPEAT
            IF Video[Search, 1] = Title
              THEN
                FOR Index1 ← 1 TO 4
                    Results[Store, Index1] ← Video[Search, Index1]
                NEXT Index1
                Store ← Store + 1
            ENDIF
            Search ← Search + 1
        UNTIL Video[Search, 1] = "" OR Search = 10000
        IF Results[1, 1] <> ""
          THEN
            OUTPUT "The results: "
            FOR Index1 ← 1 TO Store - 1
                FOR Index2 ← 1 TO 4
                    OUTPUT Results[Index1, Index2]
                NEXT Index2
            NEXT Index1
          ELSE
            OUTPUT "Item not found"
        ENDIF
    ENDIF
UNTIL Answer = 3

Q.c:
An algorithm has been written in pseudocode for a user to repeatedly input positive whole numbers and store them in an array called Values[] until –1 is input or until the array is full.
The algorithm outputs the average of the numbers to 2 decimal places.
Q.pc:
DECLARE Counter : INTEGER
DECLARE Total : INTEGER
DECLARE Average : INTEGER
DECLARE Values : ARRAY[1:100] OF INTEGER
Counter ← 1
Total ← 0
OUTPUT "Please enter a positive whole number or -1 "
INPUT Number
WHILE Number = -1 AND Counter <= 100 DO
    Values[Counter] ← Number
    Total ← Total + 1
    Counter ← Counter + 1
    INPUT Number
ENDWHILE
Counter ← Counter - 1
Average ← Counter / Total
OUTPUT "The average is ", ROUND(Average, 2)

Q.q:
A weather monitoring station records the number of minutes of sunshine for each day of a month.
The one-dimensional (1D) array Sunshine[] is used to store the number of minutes of sunshine for each day. The index of the array represents the day.
The one-dimensional (1D) array MonthDays[] contains the number of days in each month. The index of the array represents the month. In this array, 28 is stored in index 2 for the month of February. However, there are 29 days in February in a leap year.
In this program, a leap year is a year that divides by 4 with no remainder. For example, 2026 is not a leap year but 2028 will be a leap year.
Write a program that meets the following requirements:
  • allows the user to input a year, calculates whether it is a leap year and updates the number of days in February as appropriate
  • allows a user to input the name of one of the first three months of the year: January, February or March
  • allows a user to input the number of minutes of sunshine for each day of the month and validates the input
  • calculates the total amount of sunshine for the month in hours and minutes
  • finds the highest amount of daily sunshine for the month
  • outputs the: year; month; total amount of sunshine for the month in hours and minutes; the highest amount of daily sunshine for the month.
You must use pseudocode or program code and add comments to explain how your code works.
Do not declare any arrays or variables; assume that this has already been done.
All inputs and outputs must contain suitable messages.
Q.st:
// The arrays are given in the question. Test data:
DECLARE Sunshine : ARRAY[1:31] OF INTEGER
DECLARE MonthDays : ARRAY[1:12] OF INTEGER
MonthDays[1] ← 31
MonthDays[2] ← 28
MonthDays[3] ← 31
MonthDays[4] ← 30
MonthDays[5] ← 31
MonthDays[6] ← 30
MonthDays[7] ← 31
MonthDays[8] ← 31
MonthDays[9] ← 30
MonthDays[10] ← 31
MonthDays[11] ← 30
MonthDays[12] ← 31

// Write your program below

ck.lab: 2028, February (a leap year: 29 days), 28 days of 60 minutes and one of 600: total 38 hours 0 minutes
2026, February (not a leap year: 28 days), every day 30 minutes: total 14 hours 0 minutes
March: 31 days, every day 120 minutes: total 62 hours 0 minutes

pts: R1: inputs the year, calculates whether it's a leap year, updates MonthDays[] if appropriate, and inputs the month name (selection, input)
R2: inputs and validates the daily minutes for the month, calculates the total minutes and finds the highest daily sunshine (validation, iteration, selection, totalling)
R3: outputs the year, the month and the highest daily sunshine, and calculates and outputs the total sunshine in hours and minutes (output)
g: Marked in levels: AO2 (up to 9 marks) for the programming techniques and data structures used; AO3 (up to 6 marks) for comments, meaningful identifiers, logic and accuracy.
Use the array and variable names given in the scenario exactly.
All inputs and outputs need suitable messages.
ms.code:
// R1: leap year and month
Total ← 0
Max ← 0
OUTPUT "Please enter a year"
INPUT Year
IF MOD(Year, 4) = 0   // leap year: February has 29 days
  THEN
    MonthDays[2] ← 29
  ELSE
    MonthDays[2] ← 28
ENDIF
OUTPUT "Please enter January, February or March"
INPUT Month
Month1 ← LCASE(Month)   // keep the original for output
CASE OF Month1
    "january" : Days ← MonthDays[1]
    "february" : Days ← MonthDays[2]
    "march" : Days ← MonthDays[3]
ENDCASE
// R2: input and validate each day's sunshine
FOR Count ← 1 TO Days
    REPEAT
        OUTPUT "Please enter the minutes of sunshine for day ", Count
        INPUT Sun
    UNTIL Sun >= 0 AND Sun <= 1440
    Sunshine[Count] ← Sun   // store in the array
    Total ← Total + Sun     // running total
    IF Sun > Max
      THEN
        Max ← Sun   // highest so far
    ENDIF
NEXT Count
// R3: convert to hours and minutes and output
Hours ← DIV(Total, 60)
Minutes ← MOD(Total, 60)
OUTPUT "The sunshine for ", Month, " in the year ", Year
OUTPUT "Total sunshine was ", Hours, " hours and ", Minutes, " minutes"
OUTPUT "The highest daily sunshine was ", Max, " minutes"

Q.q:
A program is required to record and analyse the daily rainfall in millimetres for one year. Assume a year has 365 days.
The one-dimensional (1D) array Rainfall[] is used to store the daily rainfall measurements.
Write a program for the following requirements:
  • Initialise the array Rainfall[] to zero.
  • Input the rainfall measurement in millimetres for each day and store it in the array.
  • Calculate the following statistics after all the inputs have been made for the year: the total rainfall for the year in centimetres (1 centimetre = 10 millimetres), rounded to two decimal places; the mean average daily rainfall in millimetres, rounded to four decimal places; the total number of days with no rainfall; the longest number of consecutive days in which there was no rainfall.
  • Output all the calculated statistics with clear and appropriate messaging.
  • If the longest number of consecutive days in which there was no rainfall is 15 or more, output a message to indicate there was a drought (a long period when there is little or no rainfall).
You must use pseudocode or program code and add comments to explain how your code works.
All arrays, variables or constants used must be declared for this algorithm.
All inputs and outputs must contain suitable messages.

ck.lab: 5 mm every day except days 101 to 120: total 172.5 cm, average 4.726 mm, 20 dry days, longest dry spell 20, drought
1 mm every day: total 36.5 cm, average 1 mm, no dry days

pts: R1: declares the variables and the array, initialises the array, inputs the daily rainfall in mm for a year and stores it (declarations, initialisation, iteration, input, output)

R2: calculates the total in cm to 2 d.p., the mean in mm to 4 d.p., the number of days with no rain and the longest run of days with no rain (totalling, counting, iteration, rounding, selection, finding a maximum)
R3: outputs all the statistics, decides whether there was a drought and outputs the result (output, selection)
g: Marked in levels: AO2 (up to 9 marks) for the programming techniques and data structures used; AO3 (up to 6 marks) for comments, meaningful identifiers, logic and accuracy.
Use the array and variable names given in the scenario exactly.
All inputs and outputs need suitable messages.
ms.code:
// array and variable declarations
DECLARE Rainfall : ARRAY[1:365] OF REAL
DECLARE Index, NoRain, DryDays, MaxDryDays : INTEGER
DECLARE TotalRain, AverageRain : REAL
// initialise the array
FOR Index ← 1 TO 365
    Rainfall[Index] ← 0
NEXT Index
// input each day's rainfall
FOR Index ← 1 TO 365
    OUTPUT "Input the rainfall measurement in mm for day ", Index
    INPUT Rainfall[Index]
NEXT Index
// total and average
TotalRain ← 0
FOR Index ← 1 TO 365
    TotalRain ← TotalRain + Rainfall[Index]
NEXT Index
AverageRain ← ROUND(TotalRain / 365, 4)
TotalRain ← ROUND(TotalRain / 10, 2)   // mm to cm
// count days with no rain, and the longest dry spell
NoRain ← 0
DryDays ← 0
MaxDryDays ← 0
FOR Index ← 1 TO 365
    IF Rainfall[Index] = 0
      THEN
        NoRain ← NoRain + 1
        DryDays ← DryDays + 1
        IF DryDays > MaxDryDays
          THEN
            MaxDryDays ← DryDays
        ENDIF
      ELSE
        DryDays ← 0
    ENDIF
NEXT Index
OUTPUT "The total rainfall for the year was ", TotalRain, " cm"
OUTPUT "The average daily rainfall was ", AverageRain, " mm"
OUTPUT "The number of days with no rainfall was ", NoRain
OUTPUT "The longest period with no rainfall was ", MaxDryDays, " days"
IF MaxDryDays >= 15
  THEN
    OUTPUT "There was a drought this year"
ENDIF

Q.q:
Five rivers show signs of pollution and are to be monitored daily for a period of 30 days.
The one-dimensional (1D) array RiverNames[] stores the names of the rivers.
The two-dimensional (2D) array RiverStats[] stores the daily measurement of biological oxygen demand (BOD) for each river.
The two-dimensional (2D) array DaysCount[] stores the number of days each river is classed as moderately polluted and the number of days each river is classed as highly polluted.
The position of the data for any river is the same in all three arrays. For example, the data in index 2 of RiverStats[] belongs to the river in index 2 of RiverNames[]
Write a program for the following requirements:
  • Input and store the names of the rivers in the array RiverNames[]
  • For each river, input and store in the array RiverStats[], the daily BOD in milligrams per litre (mg / L) on each of the 30 days.
  • Once all the inputs for the 30 days have been completed, calculate and, when appropriate, store: the average daily reading for each river, rounded to two decimal places; the number of days in which the BOD reading was between 2 mg / L and 8 mg / L inclusive (moderate pollution) for each river; the number of days in which the BOD reading was greater than 8 mg / L (high pollution) for each river.
  • Output for each river, the average daily BOD readings, the number of days with moderate pollution and the number of days with high pollution.
  • Find and output the name of the river that has the most days with high pollution.
The program does not need to identify more than one river with an equally high pollution reading.
You must use pseudocode or program code and add comments to explain how your code works.
Do not declare arrays, variables or constants for this algorithm; assume this has been done.
You will need to initialise the arrays and any variables used for counting or totalling before they are used.
All inputs and outputs must contain suitable messages.

ck.lab: Every reading is 5 mg/L: each river averages 5, with 30 moderate days and 0 high days

pts: R1: initialises the arrays, inputs and stores the river names, inputs the daily BOD for 30 days and stores it (initialisation, iteration, input, output)
R2: calculates each river's average to 2 d.p., and counts the moderately and highly polluted days (totalling, counting, iteration, rounding, selection)
R3: outputs each river's average and the two counts, then finds and outputs the most polluted river (output, selection, finding the maximum)
g: Marked in levels: AO2 (up to 9 marks) for the programming techniques and data structures used; AO3 (up to 6 marks) for comments, meaningful identifiers, logic and accuracy.
Use the array and variable names given in the scenario exactly.
All inputs and outputs need suitable messages.
ms.code:
// initialise the array
FOR Index1 ← 1 TO 30
    FOR Index2 ← 1 TO 5
        RiverStats[Index1, Index2] ← 0
    NEXT Index2
NEXT Index1
// input the river names
FOR Index1 ← 1 TO 5
    OUTPUT "Input the name of river ", Index1
    INPUT RiverNames[Index1]
NEXT Index1
// input the daily BOD readings
FOR Index1 ← 1 TO 30
    OUTPUT "Day ", Index1
    FOR Index2 ← 1 TO 5
        OUTPUT "Input the reading for ", RiverNames[Index2]
        INPUT RiverStats[Index1, Index2]
    NEXT Index2
NEXT Index1
// average, moderate days and high days for each river
FOR Index1 ← 1 TO 5
    TotalBOD ← 0
    DaysCount[Index1, 1] ← 0
    DaysCount[Index1, 2] ← 0
    FOR Index2 ← 1 TO 30
        TotalBOD ← TotalBOD + RiverStats[Index2, Index1]
        IF RiverStats[Index2, Index1] >= 2 AND RiverStats[Index2, Index1] <= 8
          THEN
            DaysCount[Index1, 1] ← DaysCount[Index1, 1] + 1
        ENDIF
        IF RiverStats[Index2, Index1] > 8
          THEN
            DaysCount[Index1, 2] ← DaysCount[Index1, 2] + 1
        ENDIF
    NEXT Index2
    AverageBOD ← ROUND(TotalBOD / 30, 2)
    OUTPUT RiverNames[Index1], " has an average daily reading of ", AverageBOD
    OUTPUT "with ", DaysCount[Index1, 1], " moderately polluted days"
    OUTPUT "and ", DaysCount[Index1, 2], " highly polluted days"
NEXT Index1
// find the most polluted river
MostPollRiver ← RiverNames[1]
MostPollution ← DaysCount[1, 2]
FOR Index1 ← 2 TO 5
    IF DaysCount[Index1, 2] > MostPollution
      THEN
        MostPollution ← DaysCount[Index1, 2]
        MostPollRiver ← RiverNames[Index1]
    ENDIF
NEXT Index1
OUTPUT "The most polluted river is ", MostPollRiver

Q.q:
The one-dimensional (1D) array Clubs[] is used to store the names of 12 cricket clubs in a local sports league.
The two-dimensional (2D) array Statistics[] is used to store, for each cricket club, the number of matches won, matches drawn and matches lost.
The 1D array Points[] is used to store the total number of points each cricket club has been awarded.
The position of any cricket club’s data is the same in all three arrays. For example, the data in index 2 of Statistics[] and index 2 of Points[] belongs to the cricket club in index 2 of Clubs[]
The variable Matches stores the number of matches played by each team. Each team plays the same number of matches.
Points are awarded for: a win – 12 points; a draw – 5 points; a loss – 0 points.
Write a program that meets the following requirements:
  • allows the number of matches played to be input and stored, with a maximum of 22 matches
  • validates the number of matches played
  • allows the names of the cricket clubs to be input and stored
  • allows the number of matches won, drawn and lost to be input and stored for each team
  • validates the number of matches won, drawn or lost against the number of matches played
  • asks the user to re-enter the number of matches won, drawn or lost if the total does not match the number of matches played
  • calculates and stores the total number of points for each club
  • finds the cricket club or clubs with the highest number of points
  • outputs the name or names of the winning club or clubs, the number of wins and the total number of points awarded.
You must use pseudocode or program code and add comments to explain how your code works.
You do not need to declare any arrays or variables; you may assume that this has already been done.
All inputs and outputs must contain suitable messages.

pts: R1: inputs and stores the number of matches, the club names and the matches won, drawn and lost; validates the number of matches, and the results against the number played (prompts, iteration, variables, validation, 1D and 2D arrays)
R2: calculates and stores the points for each club; finds the highest score (calculation, finding the maximum, iteration)
R3: identifies the club(s) with the highest points, including ties, and outputs them with suitable messages (iteration, selection, output)
g: Marked in levels: AO2 (up to 9 marks) for the programming techniques and data structures used; AO3 (up to 6 marks) for comments, meaningful identifiers, logic and accuracy.
Use the array and variable names given in the scenario exactly.
All inputs and outputs need suitable messages.
The test data inputs: 30 (rejected), 22, then each club's name, wins, draws and losses.
ms.code:
// input and validate the number of matches
REPEAT
    OUTPUT "How many matches have been played (maximum 22)? "
    INPUT Matches
UNTIL Matches >= 1 AND Matches <= 22
FOR Counter ← 1 TO 12
    OUTPUT "Enter the name of the cricket club"
    INPUT Clubs[Counter]
    // input the results, checking they add up to Matches
    REPEAT
        OUTPUT "Enter the number of matches won, drawn and lost for ", Clubs[Counter]
        INPUT Won
        INPUT Drawn
        INPUT Lost
        IF Won + Drawn + Lost <> Matches
          THEN
            OUTPUT "Your inputs must total ", Matches, ", please try again"
        ENDIF
    UNTIL Won + Drawn + Lost = Matches
    Statistics[Counter, 1] ← Won
    Statistics[Counter, 2] ← Drawn
    Statistics[Counter, 3] ← Lost
    // 12 points for a win, 5 for a draw
    Points[Counter] ← Won * 12 + Drawn * 5
NEXT Counter
// find the highest points
Max ← -100
FOR Counter ← 1 TO 12
    IF Points[Counter] > Max
      THEN
        Max ← Points[Counter]
    ENDIF
NEXT Counter
// output every club with the highest points
FOR Counter ← 1 TO 12
    IF Points[Counter] = Max
      THEN
        OUTPUT "Winning club: ", Clubs[Counter]
        OUTPUT "Number of wins: ", Statistics[Counter, 1]
    ENDIF
NEXT Counter
OUTPUT "Winning points: ", Max

Q.q:
A one-player game uses the two-dimensional (2D) array Grid[] to store the location of a secret cell to be found by the player in 10 moves. Each row and column has 5 cells. The player starts at Grid[1,1], the top-left cell.
At the start of the game:
  • The program places an ‘X’ in a random cell (not in Grid[1,1]) and empties all the other cells in the grid.
  • The player starts at the top left of the grid.
  • The player has 10 moves.
During the game:
  • The player can move left, right, up or down by one cell and the move must be within the grid.
  • “You Win” is displayed if the player moves to the cell with ‘X’ and has played 10 moves or less.
  • “You Lose” is displayed if the player has made 10 moves without finding the ‘X’.
Write a program that meets these requirements.
You must use pseudocode or program code and add comments to explain how your code works.
You do not need to declare any arrays or variables; you may assume that this has already been done.
All inputs and outputs must contain suitable messages.

pts: R1: sets up the game: generates a random cell for the X, clears all the other cells, sets the player's start position and the move counter (iteration, arrays, ROUND and RANDOM)
R2: inputs each move and checks it's valid, inside the grid (input, output, iteration, selection)
R3: decides the outcome: outputs You Win if the X is found; otherwise counts the move and continues; outputs You Lose after 10 moves (arrays, iteration, selection, output)
g: Marked in levels: AO2 (up to 9 marks) for the programming techniques and data structures used; AO3 (up to 6 marks) for comments, meaningful identifiers, logic and accuracy.
Use the array and variable names given in the scenario exactly.
All inputs and outputs need suitable messages.
ms.code:
// set up the game: empty every cell
FOR Row ← 1 TO 5
    FOR Column ← 1 TO 5
        Grid[Row, Column] ← ""
    NEXT Column
NEXT Row
// place the X in a random cell that isn't Grid[1,1]
REPEAT
    XRow ← ROUND(RANDOM() * 4 + 1, 0)
    XColumn ← ROUND(RANDOM() * 4 + 1, 0)
UNTIL NOT (XRow = 1 AND XColumn = 1)
Grid[XRow, XColumn] ← "X"
NumberMoves ← 0
PlayerRow ← 1
PlayerColumn ← 1
Win ← FALSE
// play until the X is found or 10 moves are used
WHILE NumberMoves < 10 AND NOT Win DO
    OUTPUT "Enter your move: L, R, U or D"
    INPUT Move
    NewRow ← PlayerRow
    NewColumn ← PlayerColumn
    CASE OF UCASE(Move)
        "L" : NewColumn ← PlayerColumn - 1
        "R" : NewColumn ← PlayerColumn + 1
        "U" : NewRow ← PlayerRow - 1
        "D" : NewRow ← PlayerRow + 1
    ENDCASE
    // a move must stay inside the grid
    IF NewRow < 1 OR NewRow > 5 OR NewColumn < 1 OR NewColumn > 5 OR (NewRow = PlayerRow AND NewColumn = PlayerColumn)
      THEN
        OUTPUT "Invalid move, try again"
      ELSE
        PlayerRow ← NewRow
        PlayerColumn ← NewColumn
        NumberMoves ← NumberMoves + 1
        IF Grid[PlayerRow, PlayerColumn] = "X"
          THEN
            Win ← TRUE
        ENDIF
    ENDIF
ENDWHILE
IF Win
  THEN
    OUTPUT "You Win"
  ELSE
    OUTPUT "You Lose"
ENDIF

Q.q:
A one-dimensional (1D) array Teams[] contains the names of 10 football teams in a local league.
A two-dimensional (2D) array Results[] stores, for each team, the total number of games won, games drawn, games lost and points.
The position of any team’s data is the same in both arrays. For example the data in index 3 of Results[] belongs to the team in index 3 of Teams[]
The array data will be used to find the current leader of the league.
The variable Played stores the number of games played by each team. Each team plays the same number of games.
Write a program that meets the following requirements:
  • allows the number of games played to be input and stored, with a maximum of 18 games
  • allows the names of the teams to be input and stored
  • allows the number of games won, drawn and lost to be input and stored for each team
  • validates the number of games played and the number of games won, drawn or lost against the number of games played
  • calculates and stores the number of points for each team using three points for a win and one point for a draw; there are no points for a loss
  • sorts the array Results[] into descending order of number of points, ensuring the corresponding parallel array Teams[] is kept in the same order
  • determines how many teams have the highest number of points
  • outputs the name(s) of the winning team(s) along with the number of points achieved.
You must use pseudocode or program code and add comments to explain how your code works.
You do not need to declare any arrays, variables or constants; you may assume that this has already been done.
All inputs and outputs must contain suitable messages.

pts: R1: inputs and stores the games played, the teams and the games won, drawn and lost, with validation of the numbers (iteration, range check, input, output)
R2: calculates and stores the points, then sorts the arrays by points, keeping them in step (calculation, sort, nested iteration)
R3: finds and outputs the top team(s) and their points (finding the maximum, counting, output)
g: Marked in levels: AO2 (up to 9 marks) for the programming techniques and data structures used; AO3 (up to 6 marks) for comments, meaningful identifiers, logic and accuracy.
Use the array and variable names given in the scenario exactly.
All inputs and outputs need suitable messages.
The test data inputs 18, then each team's name, wins, draws and losses, one value at a time.
ms.code:
// input and validate the number of games
REPEAT
    OUTPUT "How many games have been played (maximum 18)? "
    INPUT Played
UNTIL Played >= 1 AND Played <= 18
FOR InLoop ← 1 TO 10
    OUTPUT "Enter the name of the team"
    INPUT Teams[InLoop]
    // the results must add up to the games played
    REPEAT
        OUTPUT "Enter the games won, drawn and lost for ", Teams[InLoop]
        INPUT Won
        INPUT Drawn
        INPUT Lost
        IF Won + Drawn + Lost <> Played
          THEN
            OUTPUT "Your inputs must total ", Played, ", please try again"
        ENDIF
    UNTIL Won + Drawn + Lost = Played
    Results[InLoop, 1] ← Won
    Results[InLoop, 2] ← Drawn
    Results[InLoop, 3] ← Lost
    Results[InLoop, 4] ← Won * 3 + Drawn   // 3 points a win, 1 a draw
NEXT InLoop
// bubble sort into descending order of points, keeping Teams in step
Flag ← TRUE
WHILE Flag DO
    Flag ← FALSE
    FOR Sort ← 1 TO 9
        IF Results[Sort, 4] < Results[Sort + 1, 4]
          THEN
            TempName ← Teams[Sort]
            Teams[Sort] ← Teams[Sort + 1]
            Teams[Sort + 1] ← TempName
            FOR Col ← 1 TO 4
                Temp ← Results[Sort, Col]
                Results[Sort, Col] ← Results[Sort + 1, Col]
                Results[Sort + 1, Col] ← Temp
            NEXT Col
            Flag ← TRUE
        ENDIF
    NEXT Sort
ENDWHILE
// count how many teams share the top score
Count ← 1
WHILE Count < 10 AND Results[Count + 1, 4] = Results[1, 4] DO
    Count ← Count + 1
ENDWHILE
FOR OutLoop ← 1 TO Count
    OUTPUT "Winning team: ", Teams[OutLoop]
NEXT OutLoop
OUTPUT "Winning points: ", Results[1, 4]

Q.q:
A one-dimensional (1D) array Days[] contains the names of the days of the week. A two-dimensional (2D) array Readings[] is used to store 24 temperature readings, taken once an hour, for each of the seven days of the week. A 1D array AverageTemp[] is used to store the average temperature for each day of the week.
The position of any day’s data is the same in all three arrays. For example, if Wednesday is in index 4 of Days[], Wednesday’s temperature readings are in index 4 of Readings[] and Wednesday’s average temperature is in index 4 of AverageTemp[]
The temperature readings are in Celsius to one decimal place. Temperatures can only be from –20.0 °C to +50.0 °C inclusive.
Write a program that meets the following requirements:
  • input and validate the hourly temperatures for one week
  • calculate and store the average temperature for each day of the week
  • calculate the average temperature for the whole week
  • convert all the average temperatures from Celsius to Fahrenheit by using the formula Fahrenheit = Celsius * 9 / 5 + 32
  • output the average temperature in Celsius and in Fahrenheit for each day
  • output the overall average temperature in Celsius and in Fahrenheit for the whole week.
You must use pseudocode or program code and add comments to explain how your code works.
You do not need to declare any arrays, variables or constants; you may assume that this has already been done.
All inputs and outputs must contain suitable messages.
All data output must be rounded to one decimal place.
You will need to initialise and populate the array Days[] at the start of the program.

ck.lab: Every reading is 20.0: every average is 20.0 °C and 68.0 °F
60 and -25 are rejected, then every reading is 10.0: averages 10.0 °C and 50.0 °F

pts: R1: inputs, validates and stores the hourly temperatures for each day (prompts, range check, nested iteration)
R2: calculates, rounds to 1 d.p. and stores each day's average, and calculates the week's average to 1 d.p. (iteration, totalling, rounding)
R3: converts every average to Fahrenheit (1 d.p.) and outputs the averages in Celsius and Fahrenheit with suitable messages (output, rounding)
g: Marked in levels: AO2 (up to 9 marks) for the programming techniques and data structures used; AO3 (up to 6 marks) for comments, meaningful identifiers, logic and accuracy.
Use the array and variable names given in the scenario exactly.
All inputs and outputs need suitable messages.
ms.code:
// set up the Days array
Days[1] ← "Sunday"
Days[2] ← "Monday"
Days[3] ← "Tuesday"
Days[4] ← "Wednesday"
Days[5] ← "Thursday"
Days[6] ← "Friday"
Days[7] ← "Saturday"
TotalWeekTemp ← 0
FOR WeekLoop ← 1 TO 7
    TotalDayTemp ← 0
    FOR DayLoop ← 1 TO 24
        OUTPUT "Enter temperature ", DayLoop, " for ", Days[WeekLoop]
        INPUT InTemp
        // validation: -20.0 to +50.0 inclusive
        WHILE InTemp < -20.0 OR InTemp > 50.0 DO
            OUTPUT "The temperature must be from -20.0 to +50.0. Please try again"
            INPUT InTemp
        ENDWHILE
        Readings[WeekLoop, DayLoop] ← InTemp
        TotalDayTemp ← TotalDayTemp + InTemp
    NEXT DayLoop
    AverageTemp[WeekLoop] ← ROUND(TotalDayTemp / 24, 1)
    TotalWeekTemp ← TotalWeekTemp + AverageTemp[WeekLoop]
NEXT WeekLoop
AverageWeekTemp ← ROUND(TotalWeekTemp / 7, 1)
// output in Celsius and Fahrenheit
FOR WeekLoop ← 1 TO 7
    OUTPUT "The average temperature on ", Days[WeekLoop], " was ", AverageTemp[WeekLoop], " Celsius and ", ROUND(AverageTemp[WeekLoop] * 9 / 5 + 32, 1), " Fahrenheit"
NEXT WeekLoop
OUTPUT "The average temperature for the week was ", AverageWeekTemp, " Celsius and ", ROUND(AverageWeekTemp * 9 / 5 + 32, 1), " Fahrenheit"

pts: R1: checks the account ID exists and that the name and password match (input, iteration / validation, selection, output)
R2: displays the menu and allows a choice to be made (output, input, selection)

R3: carries out the chosen action using procedures with the account ID as a parameter, updating the balance correctly and respecting the withdrawal and overdraft limits (arrays, procedures with parameters)
g: Marked in levels: AO2 (up to 9 marks) for the programming techniques and data structures used; AO3 (up to 6 marks) for comments, meaningful identifiers, logic and accuracy.
Use the array and variable names given in the scenario exactly.
All inputs and outputs need suitable messages.
ms.code:
DECLARE Valid : BOOLEAN // global, set by CheckDetails
DECLARE AccountNumber, Choice : INTEGER

PROCEDURE CheckDetails(AccID : INTEGER)
    DECLARE Name, Password : STRING // local variables
    Valid ← FALSE
    IF AccID < 1 OR AccID > Size
      THEN
        OUTPUT "Invalid account number"
      ELSE
        OUTPUT "Please enter your name "
        INPUT Name
        OUTPUT "Please enter your password "
        INPUT Password
        // name and password must both match the stored values
        IF Name = Account[AccID, 1] AND Password = Account[AccID, 2]
          THEN
            Valid ← TRUE
          ELSE
            OUTPUT "Invalid name or password"
        ENDIF
    ENDIF
ENDPROCEDURE

PROCEDURE Balance(AccID : INTEGER)
    OUTPUT "Your balance is ", AccDetails[AccID, 1]
ENDPROCEDURE

PROCEDURE Withdrawal(AccID : INTEGER)
    DECLARE Amount : REAL // local variable
    OUTPUT "Please enter the amount to withdraw "
    INPUT Amount
    IF Amount <= 0
      THEN
        OUTPUT "The amount must be positive"
      ELSE
        IF Amount > AccDetails[AccID, 3]
          THEN
            OUTPUT "Amount is greater than your withdrawal limit"
          ELSE
            // the balance may not go below minus the overdraft limit
            IF AccDetails[AccID, 1] - Amount < -AccDetails[AccID, 2]
              THEN
                OUTPUT "This would take you past your overdraft limit"
              ELSE
                AccDetails[AccID, 1] ← AccDetails[AccID, 1] - Amount
                OUTPUT "Withdrawal complete"
            ENDIF
        ENDIF
    ENDIF
ENDPROCEDURE

PROCEDURE Deposit(AccID : INTEGER)
    DECLARE Amount : REAL // local variable
    REPEAT
        OUTPUT "Please enter a positive amount to deposit "
        INPUT Amount
    UNTIL Amount > 0
    AccDetails[AccID, 1] ← AccDetails[AccID, 1] + Amount
ENDPROCEDURE

// main program
OUTPUT "Please enter your account number "
INPUT AccountNumber
CALL CheckDetails(AccountNumber)
IF Valid
  THEN
    REPEAT
        OUTPUT "1. display balance"
        OUTPUT "2. withdraw money"
        OUTPUT "3. deposit money"
        OUTPUT "4. exit"
        OUTPUT "Please choose 1, 2, 3 or 4"
        INPUT Choice
        CASE OF Choice
            1 : CALL Balance(AccountNumber)
            2 : CALL Withdrawal(AccountNumber)
            3 : CALL Deposit(AccountNumber)
            4 : OUTPUT "Goodbye"
            OTHERWISE OUTPUT "Invalid choice"
        ENDCASE
    UNTIL Choice = 4
ENDIF

Q.q:
A two-dimensional (2D) array Contacts[] is used to store names and telephone numbers. All the data is stored as strings. The array must have the capacity to store 100 contacts in the form of:
  • column 1 – contact names as: last name, first name, for example: Smith, John
  • column 2 – telephone numbers.
The variable CurrentSize shows how many contacts are in the array.
Write a program that meets the following requirements:
  • display a menu of choices: enter new contact details; display all the contact details; delete all the contact details
  • validate the menu input
  • allow up to a maximum of five new contacts to be added to the array at any one time
  • do not allow more than 100 contacts in total
  • after new contacts have been added, sort the array by contact name, as long as there are at least two contacts in the array
  • output the whole of the array
  • delete the contents of the array.
You must use pseudocode or program code and add comments to explain how your code works.
You do not need to declare any arrays, variables or constants; you may assume that this has already been done.
All inputs and outputs must contain suitable messages.
You do not need to initialise the data in the array Contacts[] and the variable CurrentSize

ck.lab: Add Smith then Adams, then display: Adams is listed first
Add Patel, later add Brown, then display: still sorted
Menu choice 7 and a request for 6 contacts are both rejected

pts: R1: outputs the menu and inputs the choice, with validation (range check, output with messages, input with prompts)

R2: inputs the number of new contacts within the limits, inputs the new data, updates CurrentSize and sorts the array when there are at least two contacts (range check, totalling, iteration, bubble sort)
R3: outputs the whole contents of the array and deletes the contents of the array (iteration, output with messages, array initialisation)
g: Marked in levels: AO2 (up to 9 marks) for the programming techniques and data structures used; AO3 (up to 6 marks) for comments, meaningful identifiers, logic and accuracy.
Use the array and variable names given in the scenario exactly.
All inputs and outputs need suitable messages.
ms.code:
// the program keeps running until it is closed
Cont ← TRUE
WHILE Cont DO
    // display the menu
    OUTPUT "Press 1 to enter new contacts"
    OUTPUT "Press 2 to display your contacts"
    OUTPUT "Press 3 to delete all contacts"
    INPUT Choice
    // validate the choice as 1, 2 or 3
    WHILE Choice < 1 OR Choice > 3 DO
        OUTPUT "Incorrect entry - please enter 1, 2 or 3"
        INPUT Choice
    ENDWHILE
    IF Choice = 1
      THEN
        IF CurrentSize = 100
          THEN
            OUTPUT "Your contacts are full"
          ELSE
            OUTPUT "How many contacts (1 to 5)?"
            INPUT NewContacts
            // between 1 and 5, and not more than the space left
            WHILE NewContacts < 1 OR NewContacts > 5 OR CurrentSize + NewContacts > 100 DO
                OUTPUT "You may enter 1 to 5 contacts, and at most ", 100 - CurrentSize, " more"
                INPUT NewContacts
            ENDWHILE
            FOR Count ← CurrentSize + 1 TO CurrentSize + NewContacts
                OUTPUT "Enter the contact name as last name, first name"
                INPUT Contacts[Count, 1]
                OUTPUT "Enter the telephone number"
                INPUT Contacts[Count, 2]
            NEXT Count
            CurrentSize ← CurrentSize + NewContacts
            // bubble sort by name if there are at least two contacts
            IF CurrentSize >= 2
              THEN
                REPEAT
                    Flag ← FALSE
                    FOR Count ← 1 TO CurrentSize - 1
                        IF Contacts[Count + 1, 1] < Contacts[Count, 1]
                          THEN
                            Flag ← TRUE
                            FOR Count2 ← 1 TO 2
                                Temp ← Contacts[Count, Count2]
                                Contacts[Count, Count2] ← Contacts[Count + 1, Count2]
                                Contacts[Count + 1, Count2] ← Temp
                            NEXT Count2
                        ENDIF
                    NEXT Count
                UNTIL NOT Flag
            ENDIF
        ENDIF
    ENDIF
    // display all the contacts
    IF Choice = 2
      THEN
        OUTPUT "Name and telephone number"
        FOR Count ← 1 TO CurrentSize
            OUTPUT Contacts[Count, 1], "   ", Contacts[Count, 2]
        NEXT Count
    ENDIF
    // delete all the contacts
    IF Choice = 3
      THEN
        FOR Count ← 1 TO 100
            FOR Count2 ← 1 TO 2
                Contacts[Count, Count2] ← ""
            NEXT Count2
        NEXT Count
        CurrentSize ← 0
        OUTPUT "All contacts deleted"
    ENDIF
ENDWHILE

        WHILE Counter < NumSeats DO

  • input the choice of wood and find its price per square metre
  • calculate the price of the wood needed
  • store all data in the relevant array
  • output the customer’s quotation to include: the name of the customer, the choice of wood and the calculated price of the wood required
  • continue to accept the next customer.
You must use pseudocode or program code and add comments to explain how your code works.

R2: initialises the wood arrays; calculates the area (rounded up); inputs the wood choice, finds its price and calculates the cost; stores all the data in the relevant arrays (array initialisation, rounding, retrieval from arrays, calculation and storage)
R3: outputs the customer name, wood choice and price with messages, and continues for the next customer (output with messages, iteration of the whole program)
g: Marked in levels: AO2 (up to 9 marks) for the programming techniques and data structures used; AO3 (up to 6 marks) for comments, meaningful identifiers, logic and accuracy.

WoodType[2] ← "Pine"
WoodType[3] ← "Oak"
Price[1] ← 29.99
Price[2] ← 39.99
Price[3] ← 54.99
CurrentCustomer ← 1
// keep going for the next customer
WHILE TRUE DO
    OUTPUT "Input the customer's name "
    INPUT Customers[CurrentCustomer]
    // input and validate the room length
    OUTPUT "What is the length of the room? "
    INPUT RoomLength
    WHILE RoomLength < 1.5 OR RoomLength > 10.0 DO
        OUTPUT "The measurement must be from 1.5 to 10.0, please try again "
        INPUT RoomLength
    ENDWHILE
    // input and validate the room width
    OUTPUT "What is the width of the room? "
    INPUT RoomWidth
    WHILE RoomWidth < 1.5 OR RoomWidth > 10.0 DO
        OUTPUT "The measurement must be from 1.5 to 10.0, please try again "
        INPUT RoomWidth
    ENDWHILE
    // area rounded up to the next whole number
    RoomArea ← ROUND(RoomLength, 1) * ROUND(RoomWidth, 1)
    WholeArea ← ROUND(RoomArea, 0)
    IF WholeArea < RoomArea
      THEN
        WholeArea ← WholeArea + 1
    ENDIF
    // show the wood choices and input one

        OUTPUT Count, " ", WoodType[Count], " $", Price[Count]
    NEXT Count
    OUTPUT "Input a number from 1 to 3 "
    INPUT WoodChoice
    WHILE WoodChoice < 1 OR WoodChoice > 3 DO
        OUTPUT "Your input is out of range, please try again "
        INPUT WoodChoice
    ENDWHILE
    WoodCost ← ROUND(WholeArea * Price[WoodChoice], 2)
    // store the quotation
    Quotations[CurrentCustomer, 1] ← RoomLength
    Quotations[CurrentCustomer, 2] ← RoomWidth
    Quotations[CurrentCustomer, 3] ← WholeArea
    Quotations[CurrentCustomer, 4] ← WoodChoice
    Quotations[CurrentCustomer, 5] ← WoodCost
    // output the quotation
    OUTPUT "Customer name: ", Customers[CurrentCustomer]
    OUTPUT "The wood you have chosen is: ", WoodType[WoodChoice]
    OUTPUT "Your total price is: $", WoodCost
    // ready for the next customer (back to the start when the array is full)
    CurrentCustomer ← CurrentCustomer + 1
    IF CurrentCustomer > 100
      THEN
        CurrentCustomer ← 1
    ENDIF
ENDWHILE

Q.q:
A weather station takes temperature readings once an hour for a week. These temperatures are stored in a two-dimensional (2D) array Temperatures[]
Each column contains 24 readings for a single day. The first temperature is recorded at 00:00 and the final temperature at 23:00. There are seven columns, one for each day of the week, starting with Monday and ending with Sunday.
The variables MaxDay, MinDay and AvDay are used to store the maximum, minimum, and average temperatures for a day. The variables MaxWeek, MinWeek and AvWeek are used to store the maximum, minimum, and average temperatures for the week.
The array has already been set up and the data stored.
Write a program that meets the following requirements:
  • finds the maximum and minimum temperatures for each day
  • calculates the average temperature for each day
  • outputs for each day: the name of the day (for example Monday), the maximum temperature, the minimum temperature and the average temperature
  • finds the maximum and minimum temperatures for the week
  • calculates the average temperature for the week
  • outputs the maximum, minimum and average temperatures for the week.
All temperatures output must be rounded to two decimal places.
You must use pseudocode or program code and add comments to explain how your code works.
All inputs and outputs must contain suitable messages.
You do not need to declare any arrays or variables; you may assume that this has already been done.
You do not need to initialise the data in the array Temperatures[]

ck.lab: Every reading is 12.5: every maximum, minimum and average is 12.5
ck.pre:
DECLARE Temperatures : ARRAY[1:24, 1:7] OF REAL
// test data
FOR H ← 1 TO 24
    FOR D ← 1 TO 7
        Temperatures[H, D] ← 12.5
    NEXT D
NEXT H

ck.lab: Varied readings: each day's max, min and average in order, then the week's
ck.pre:
DECLARE Temperatures : ARRAY[1:24, 1:7] OF REAL
// test data
FOR H ← 1 TO 24
    FOR D ← 1 TO 7
        Temperatures[H, D] ← MOD(H * 7 + D * 13, 30) / 2 - 3 + D
    NEXT D
NEXT H

ck.lab: Readings that are all below zero (–5 – the day number)
ck.pre:
DECLARE Temperatures : ARRAY[1:24, 1:7] OF REAL
// test data
FOR H ← 1 TO 24
    FOR D ← 1 TO 7
        Temperatures[H, D] ← -5 - D
    NEXT D
NEXT H

pts: R1: finds the maximum and minimum temperatures for each day and calculates the daily average (searching, totalling)
R2: finds the maximum and minimum temperatures for the week and calculates the weekly average (nested searching, totalling)
R3: outputs each day's name with its rounded maximum, minimum and average, and the rounded maximum, minimum and average for the week (output with messages, rounding)
g: Marked in levels: AO2 (up to 9 marks) for the programming techniques and data structures used; AO3 (up to 6 marks) for comments, meaningful identifiers, logic and accuracy.
Use the array and variable names given in the scenario exactly.
All inputs and outputs need suitable messages.
ms.code:
DECLARE Days : ARRAY[1:7] OF STRING
Days[1] ← "Monday"
Days[2] ← "Tuesday"
Days[3] ← "Wednesday"
Days[4] ← "Thursday"
Days[5] ← "Friday"
Days[6] ← "Saturday"
Days[7] ← "Sunday"
// initialise the values for the week
MaxWeek ← -1000
MinWeek ← 1000
WeekTotal ← 0
FOR Day ← 1 TO 7
    // initialise the values for this day
    MaxDay ← -1000
    MinDay ← 1000
    DayTotal ← 0
    FOR Hour ← 1 TO 24
        DayTotal ← DayTotal + Temperatures[Hour, Day]
        IF Temperatures[Hour, Day] > MaxDay
          THEN
            MaxDay ← Temperatures[Hour, Day]
        ENDIF
        IF Temperatures[Hour, Day] < MinDay
          THEN
            MinDay ← Temperatures[Hour, Day]
        ENDIF
    NEXT Hour
    AvDay ← DayTotal / 24
    // output the results for the day
    OUTPUT Days[Day]
    OUTPUT "Maximum temperature ", ROUND(MaxDay, 2)
    OUTPUT "Minimum temperature ", ROUND(MinDay, 2)
    OUTPUT "Average temperature ", ROUND(AvDay, 2)
    // update the values for the week
    IF MaxDay > MaxWeek
      THEN
        MaxWeek ← MaxDay
    ENDIF
    IF MinDay < MinWeek
      THEN
        MinWeek ← MinDay
    ENDIF
    WeekTotal ← WeekTotal + DayTotal
NEXT Day
AvWeek ← WeekTotal / (24 * 7)
OUTPUT "Maximum temperature for the week ", ROUND(MaxWeek, 2)
OUTPUT "Minimum temperature for the week ", ROUND(MinWeek, 2)
OUTPUT "Average temperature for the week ", ROUND(AvWeek, 2)

pts: R1: inputs and verifies the members' times (input, iteration)
R2: sorts both arrays into ascending order of time and outputs the top three members and their times as First, Second and Third (nested iteration, sorting, selection, output)
R3: stores the names of the members who get a certificate and outputs the number of certificates (iteration, selection, counting, output)
g: Marked in levels: AO2 (up to 9 marks) for the programming techniques and data structures used; AO3 (up to 6 marks) for comments, meaningful identifiers, logic and accuracy.
Use the array and variable names given in the scenario exactly.
All inputs and outputs need suitable messages.
ms.code:
DECLARE Position : ARRAY[1:3] OF STRING
Position[1] ← "First"
Position[2] ← "Second"
Position[3] ← "Third"
// input each member's time twice and check the two inputs match
FOR Index ← 1 TO 200
    REPEAT
        OUTPUT "Please enter the time for ", MemberName[Index]
        INPUT Time1
        OUTPUT "Please re-enter the time"
        INPUT Time2
        IF Time1 <> Time2
          THEN
            OUTPUT "The two times don't match, please try again"
        ENDIF
    UNTIL Time1 = Time2
    MemberTime[Index] ← Time1
NEXT Index
// bubble sort both arrays into ascending order of time
Last ← 199
REPEAT
    Swap ← FALSE
    FOR Index ← 1 TO Last
        IF MemberTime[Index] > MemberTime[Index + 1]
          THEN
            TempTime ← MemberTime[Index]
            MemberTime[Index] ← MemberTime[Index + 1]
            MemberTime[Index + 1] ← TempTime
            TempName ← MemberName[Index]
            MemberName[Index] ← MemberName[Index + 1]
            MemberName[Index + 1] ← TempName
            Swap ← TRUE
        ENDIF
    NEXT Index
    Last ← Last - 1
UNTIL NOT Swap OR Last = 0
// output the top three
FOR Index ← 1 TO 3
    OUTPUT Position[Index], ": ", MemberName[Index], " with a time of ", MemberTime[Index], " seconds"
NEXT Index
// store the names of members who get a certificate
Count ← 0
FOR Index ← 1 TO 200
    IF MemberTime[Index] < 240
      THEN
        Count ← Count + 1
        MemberCertificate[Count] ← MemberName[Index]
    ENDIF
NEXT Index
OUTPUT "Number of certificates to be printed is ", Count

DECLARE ItemList : ARRAY[1:100] OF STRING
DECLARE Counter : STRING
DECLARE Limit : INTEGER
DECLARE Pass : INTEGER
DECLARE Swapped : BOOLEAN
DECLARE Temp : STRING
Limit ← 100
Pass ← 1
Temp ← TRUE
WHILE Swapped = TRUE OR Pass <= Limit - 1 DO
    Swapped ← FALSE
    FOR Counter ← 1 TO Limit - Pass
        IF ItemList[Counter] > ItemList[Counter + 1]
          THEN
            Temp ← ItemList[Counter]
            ItemList[Counter] ← ItemList[Counter + 1]
            ItemList[Counter] ← Temp
            Swapped ← TRUE
        ENDCASE
        Pass ← Pass + 1
    NEXT Counter
ENDWHILE

A two-dimensional (2D) array Dimensions[] is used to store the length, width and area of each room.
The position of any room’s data is the same in both arrays. For example, the data in index 5 of Dimensions[] belongs to the room in index 5 of Rooms[]

Write a program that meets the following requirements:
  • allows the number of rooms for which data is required to be input, stored and validated
  • allows the name of the room and the length and width of the room, in metres, to be entered and stored
  • allows the area of each room to be calculated as length multiplied by width and stored as square metres rounded to two decimal places
  • calculates the average size of all the rooms by area, in square metres, rounded to two decimal places
  • finds the largest room and smallest room by area
  • outputs the names of all rooms with their dimensions and area
  • outputs the names of the largest room and smallest room by area
  • outputs the total area of the house and the average size of all the rooms by area.
You must use pseudocode or program code and add comments to explain how your code works.
You do not need to declare any arrays or variables; you may assume that this has already been done.
All inputs and outputs must contain suitable messages.

ck.lab: 3 rooms: areas 14.7, 22 and 4.37; Lounge largest, Bath smallest; total 41.07, average 13.69
2 and 21 rooms are rejected before 3 is accepted
4 rooms where the first is the largest: Hall 6 × 5 = 30 is largest, Store 1.5 × 1.2 = 1.8 smallest

pts: R1: inputs and stores the number of rooms (validated 3 to 20), the room names and dimensions (input with prompts, iteration, 1D and 2D arrays, validation)
R2: calculates and stores each room's area (2 d.p.), the total area and the average area (2 d.p.), and finds the largest and smallest rooms (calculation, totalling, rounding, max and min, iteration)
R3: outputs the room names with dimensions and areas, the largest and smallest rooms, the total area and the average area (iteration, output with messages)
g: Marked in levels: AO2 (up to 9 marks) for the programming techniques and data structures used; AO3 (up to 6 marks) for comments, meaningful identifiers, logic and accuracy.
Use the array and variable names given in the scenario exactly.
All inputs and outputs need suitable messages.
ms.code:
// input and validate the number of rooms (3 to 20)
REPEAT
    OUTPUT "How many rooms are in your house (3 to 20)? "
    INPUT Number
    IF Number < 3 OR Number > 20
      THEN
        OUTPUT "The number of rooms must be from 3 to 20, please try again"
    ENDIF
UNTIL Number >= 3 AND Number <= 20
// input each room's name and dimensions, and work out its area
FOR Room ← 1 TO Number
    OUTPUT "Enter the name of room ", Room
    INPUT Rooms[Room]
    OUTPUT "Enter the length of the room in metres"
    INPUT Dimensions[Room, 1]
    OUTPUT "Enter the width of the room in metres"
    INPUT Dimensions[Room, 2]
    Dimensions[Room, 3] ← ROUND(Dimensions[Room, 1] * Dimensions[Room, 2], 2)
NEXT Room
// total area, average area, largest and smallest rooms
TotalArea ← 0
Largest ← 1
Smallest ← 1
FOR Room ← 1 TO Number
    TotalArea ← TotalArea + Dimensions[Room, 3]
    IF Dimensions[Room, 3] > Dimensions[Largest, 3]
      THEN
        Largest ← Room
    ENDIF
    IF Dimensions[Room, 3] < Dimensions[Smallest, 3]
      THEN
        Smallest ← Room
    ENDIF
NEXT Room
AverageArea ← ROUND(TotalArea / Number, 2)
// output the results
FOR Room ← 1 TO Number
    OUTPUT "Room: ", Rooms[Room], "  Length: ", Dimensions[Room, 1], " m  Width: ", Dimensions[Room, 2], " m  Area: ", Dimensions[Room, 3], " square metres"
NEXT Room
OUTPUT "The largest room is: ", Rooms[Largest]
OUTPUT "The smallest room is: ", Rooms[Smallest]
OUTPUT "The total area of the house is: ", TotalArea, " square metres"
OUTPUT "The average area of the rooms is: ", AverageArea, " square metres"

DECLARE Position : ARRAY[1:2] OF STRING
Position[1] ← "Best in Group"
Position[2] ← "Second best in Group"
// input and validate each member's weight (must be more than 0)
FOR Index ← 1 TO GroupSize
    OUTPUT "Please enter the weight picked by ", PickerName[Index]
    INPUT PickedWeight[Index]
    WHILE PickedWeight[Index] <= 0 DO
        OUTPUT "The weight must be more than 0 kg, please try again"
        INPUT PickedWeight[Index]
    ENDWHILE
NEXT Index
// bubble sort both arrays into descending order of weight
Last ← GroupSize - 1
REPEAT
    Swap ← FALSE
    FOR Index ← 1 TO Last
        IF PickedWeight[Index] < PickedWeight[Index + 1]
          THEN
            TempWeight ← PickedWeight[Index]
            PickedWeight[Index] ← PickedWeight[Index + 1]
            PickedWeight[Index + 1] ← TempWeight
            TempName ← PickerName[Index]
            PickerName[Index] ← PickerName[Index + 1]
            PickerName[Index + 1] ← TempName
            Swap ← TRUE
        ENDIF
    NEXT Index
    Last ← Last - 1
UNTIL NOT Swap OR Last = 0
// output the two heaviest picks
FOR Index ← 1 TO 2
    OUTPUT Position[Index], ": ", PickerName[Index], " with a weight of ", PickedWeight[Index], " kg"
NEXT Index
// the array is sorted, so the certificates go to the members at the start
Count ← 0
FOR Index ← 1 TO GroupSize
    IF PickedWeight[Index] > 3
      THEN
        Count ← Count + 1
        PickerCertificate[Count] ← PickerName[Index]
    ENDIF
NEXT Index
OUTPUT "Number of certificates to be printed is ", Count

Q.q:
A first name is used as the search key in the algorithm. If the name is found, all the data for that name is output and the algorithm stops searching.
Explain why the given algorithm may not always give the expected results.
Q.c: This pseudocode algorithm is intended to input a first name from a user and search for it in a two-dimensional (2D) array. If the name is found, the algorithm outputs all the remaining details for that name. The algorithm will continue to allow other names to be entered for searching, until the user input stops it.
Q.pc:
DECLARE Contacts : ARRAY[1:500, 1:4] OF REAL
DECLARE Row : INTEGER
DECLARE Column : INTEGER
DECLARE Continue : BOOLEAN
DECLARE Stop : BOOLEAN
DECLARE FirstName : STRING
Continue ← TRUE
Stop ← FALSE
WHILE Continue
    Row ← 1
    OUTPUT "Enter a first name "
    OUTPUT FirstName
    REPEAT
        IF Contacts[Row, 1] = FirstName
          THEN
            FOR Column ← 1 TO 4
                OUTPUT Contacts[Row, 1]
            NEXT Column
            Stop ← TRUE
          ELSE
            Row ← Row + 1
        ENDIF
    NEXT Stop OR Row > 500
    OUTPUT "Search for another name? (Y or N)"
    INPUT Answer
    IF Answer = 'N' OR Answer = 'n'
      THEN
        Continue ← TRUE
    ENDIF
ENDWHILE

pts: There may be more than one person with the given first name // the name may not be in the array
The search stops at the first match, so it may output the data for the wrong person
If the name isn't there, there's no output (no message)

Q.q:
A program is required to test the fairness of the random number generator.
The one-dimensional (1D) array RandomNumber[] is used to store 100 000 random integers.
The two-dimensional (2D) array CountedNumber[] is used to store the integers 1 to 10, inclusive, and the frequency of each integer (the number of times each integer was generated).
Write a program that meets the following requirements:
  • Generate 100 000 random integers between 1 and 10, inclusive.
  • Store each integer in the appropriate array.
  • Calculate the frequency of each of the integers 1 to 10 and store these values in the appropriate array.
  • Sort the contents of the counted number array in descending order of frequency.
  • Calculate the chance of generating each of the integers 1 to 10, rounded to four decimal places. Use the formula: chance = frequency / 100000
  • Output each of the integers 1 to 10 in the order they are stored in the counted number array, along with the chance of generating them.
This is an example of an algorithm that sorts a 2D array into ascending order:
F ← TRUE
WHILE F DO
    F ← FALSE
    FOR I ← 1 TO 9
        IF A[I, 2] > A[I + 1, 2]
          THEN
            T1 ← A[I, 1]
            T2 ← A[I, 2]
            A[I, 1] ← A[I + 1, 1]
            A[I, 2] ← A[I + 1, 2]
            A[I + 1, 1] ← T1
            A[I + 1, 2] ← T2
            F ← TRUE
        ENDIF
    NEXT I
ENDWHILE
You must use pseudocode or program code and add comments to explain how your code works.
All arrays, variables or constants used must be declared for this algorithm.
All inputs and outputs must contain suitable messages.

pts: R1: declares the arrays and variables, then generates 100 000 random integers from 1 to 10 and stores them in an array (declarations, iteration, random numbers, rounding, storage)
R2: counts the frequency of each integer and stores the results in an array, then sorts them into descending order of frequency (initialisation, selection, counting, sorting, nested iteration)
R3: calculates the chance of each integer to 4 d.p. and outputs the results (iteration, rounding, output)
g: Marked in levels: AO2 (up to 9 marks) for the programming techniques and data structures used; AO3 (up to 6 marks) for comments, meaningful identifiers, logic and accuracy.
Use the array and variable names given in the scenario exactly.
All inputs and outputs need suitable messages.
ms.code:
// array and variable declarations
CONSTANT HowMany ← 100000
DECLARE RandomNumber : ARRAY[1:100000] OF INTEGER
DECLARE CountedNumber : ARRAY[1:10, 1:2] OF INTEGER
DECLARE Index, Value, Temp1, Temp2 : INTEGER
DECLARE Swap : BOOLEAN
// set up the counted number array: the integers 1 to 10, each with a frequency of 0
FOR Index ← 1 TO 10
    CountedNumber[Index, 1] ← Index
    CountedNumber[Index, 2] ← 0
NEXT Index
// generate and store the random integers, counting each one as it's made
FOR Index ← 1 TO HowMany
    Value ← ROUND(RANDOM() * 9, 0) + 1
    RandomNumber[Index] ← Value
    CountedNumber[Value, 2] ← CountedNumber[Value, 2] + 1
NEXT Index
// sort into descending order of frequency (stops when a pass makes no swaps)
Swap ← TRUE
WHILE Swap DO
    Swap ← FALSE
    FOR Index ← 1 TO 9
        IF CountedNumber[Index, 2] < CountedNumber[Index + 1, 2]
          THEN
            Temp1 ← CountedNumber[Index, 1]
            Temp2 ← CountedNumber[Index, 2]
            CountedNumber[Index, 1] ← CountedNumber[Index + 1, 1]
            CountedNumber[Index, 2] ← CountedNumber[Index + 1, 2]
            CountedNumber[Index + 1, 1] ← Temp1
            CountedNumber[Index + 1, 2] ← Temp2
            Swap ← TRUE
        ENDIF
    NEXT Index
ENDWHILE
// output each integer with its chance, rounded to 4 decimal places
FOR Index ← 1 TO 10
    OUTPUT "The chance of ", CountedNumber[Index, 1], " is ", ROUND(CountedNumber[Index, 2] / HowMany, 4)
NEXT Index

Q.q:
A number game has two players. Random whole numbers are generated for each player. The numbers are compared and players are given points based on the result of the comparison.
The two-dimensional (2D) array NumberGenerated[] stores each number generated for each player. The first dimension stores the player number and the second dimension stores the random whole numbers generated.
The game is played as follows:
  • 100 random whole numbers between 1 and 6 inclusive are generated for player 1 and stored in the array.
  • 100 random whole numbers between 1 and 6 inclusive are generated for player 2 and stored in the array.
  • The first number generated for each player is compared and the player with the higher number is awarded 2 points. If the two numbers are the same, both players are awarded 1 point each.
  • The comparisons repeat for all 100 numbers generated.
  • The player with the higher total number of points is output as the winner.
  • If the players have the same total number of points, a new random whole number is generated for each player and compared. This is repeated until one player has a higher number than the other player. 2 points are added to that player’s total number of points, making this player the winner.
Write a program that meets the following requirements:
  • input and validate the names of the two players
  • generate 100 random whole numbers between 1 and 6 inclusive for each player and store them in the array NumberGenerated[]
  • calculate and store the total number of points for each player
  • output the name and total number of points for each player in descending order of total number of points.
You must use pseudocode or program code and add comments to explain how your code works.
You do not need to declare any arrays or variables; assume that this has already been done.
All outputs must contain suitable messages.

ck.lab: Runs to the end with the names Ana and Ben (the numbers are random, so the result changes each time)

pts: R1: inputs and validates the names of the players (iteration, input, output)
R2: generates the random numbers for each player, and calculates and stores each player's points (iteration, totalling, selection)
R3: finds and outputs the name and points of each player in descending order, dealing with a draw (iteration, selection, output)
g: Marked in levels: AO2 (up to 9 marks) for the programming techniques and data structures used; AO3 (up to 6 marks) for comments, meaningful identifiers, logic and accuracy.
Use the array and variable names given in the scenario exactly.
All inputs and outputs need suitable messages.
ms.code:
DECLARE Points : ARRAY[1:2] OF INTEGER
DECLARE Player : ARRAY[1:2] OF STRING
// input and validate the names (presence check)
FOR P ← 1 TO 2
    OUTPUT "Please enter the name of player ", P
    INPUT Player[P]
    WHILE Player[P] = "" DO
        OUTPUT "You must enter a name, try again "
        INPUT Player[P]
    ENDWHILE
    Points[P] ← 0
NEXT P
// generate 100 random whole numbers from 1 to 6 for each player
FOR P ← 1 TO 2
    FOR Turn ← 1 TO 100
        NumberGenerated[P, Turn] ← ROUND(RANDOM() * 5, 0) + 1
    NEXT Turn
NEXT P
// compare the numbers: 2 points for the higher, 1 point each for a tie
FOR Turn ← 1 TO 100
    IF NumberGenerated[1, Turn] > NumberGenerated[2, Turn]
      THEN
        Points[1] ← Points[1] + 2
      ELSE
        IF NumberGenerated[1, Turn] < NumberGenerated[2, Turn]
          THEN
            Points[2] ← Points[2] + 2
          ELSE
            Points[1] ← Points[1] + 1
            Points[2] ← Points[2] + 1
        ENDIF
    ENDIF
NEXT Turn
// break a tie with new numbers until they are different
IF Points[1] = Points[2]
  THEN
    REPEAT
        N1 ← ROUND(RANDOM() * 5, 0) + 1
        N2 ← ROUND(RANDOM() * 5, 0) + 1
    UNTIL N1 <> N2
    IF N1 > N2
      THEN
        Points[1] ← Points[1] + 2
      ELSE
        Points[2] ← Points[2] + 2
    ENDIF
ENDIF
// output in descending order of points
IF Points[1] > Points[2]
  THEN
    OUTPUT "First: ", Player[1], " with ", Points[1], " points"
    OUTPUT "Second: ", Player[2], " with ", Points[2], " points"
  ELSE
    OUTPUT "First: ", Player[2], " with ", Points[2], " points"
    OUTPUT "Second: ", Player[1], " with ", Points[1], " points"
ENDIF

pts: R1: calculates the total points for every team over all the matches (nested iteration, totalling)
R2: counts and outputs, with each team's name, its away wins, home wins, draws and losses (nested iteration, counting, output)
R3: finds and outputs the names of the teams with the highest and lowest points (selection, output)
g: Marked in levels: AO2 (up to 9 marks) for the programming techniques and data structures used; AO3 (up to 6 marks) for comments, meaningful identifiers, logic and accuracy.

ms.code:
DECLARE TotalPoints : ARRAY[1:LeagueSize] OF INTEGER
FOR Team ← 1 TO LeagueSize
    // reset the totals for this team
    TotalPoints[Team] ← 0
    AwayWins ← 0
    HomeWins ← 0
    Draws ← 0
    Losses ← 0
    FOR Match ← 1 TO MatchNo
        TotalPoints[Team] ← TotalPoints[Team] + TeamPoints[Team, Match]
        // count each kind of result
        CASE OF TeamPoints[Team, Match]
            3 : AwayWins ← AwayWins + 1
            2 : HomeWins ← HomeWins + 1
            1 : Draws ← Draws + 1
            0 : Losses ← Losses + 1
        ENDCASE
    NEXT Match
    OUTPUT "Team: ", TeamName[Team]
    OUTPUT "Total points: ", TotalPoints[Team]
    OUTPUT "Away wins: ", AwayWins, ", home wins: ", HomeWins, ", draws: ", Draws, ", lost: ", Losses
    // keep track of the highest and lowest totals
    IF Team = 1
      THEN
        Top ← 1
        Bottom ← 1
      ELSE
        IF TotalPoints[Team] > TotalPoints[Top]
          THEN
            Top ← Team
        ENDIF
        IF TotalPoints[Team] < TotalPoints[Bottom]
          THEN
            Bottom ← Team
        ENDIF
    ENDIF
NEXT Team
OUTPUT "Team with the highest points: ", TeamName[Top]
OUTPUT "Team with the lowest points: ", TeamName[Bottom]

Q.q:
Students in a class are recording the amount of time in minutes spent in front of a screen for each day of the week.
The one-dimensional (1D) array StudentName[] contains the names of the students in the class. The two-dimensional (2D) array ScreenTime[] is used to input the number of minutes on each day spent in front of a screen.
The position of each student’s data in the two arrays is the same. For example, the student stored at index 10 in StudentName[] and ScreenTime[] is the same.
The variable ClassSize contains the number of students in the class.
Write a program that meets these requirements:
  • allows all the students to enter their daily minutes of screen times for the past week
  • calculates the total number of minutes of screen time for each student in the week
  • counts, for each student, the number of days with more than 300 minutes of screen time
  • calculates the average weekly minutes of screen time for the whole class
  • finds the student with the lowest weekly minutes of screen time
  • outputs for each student: name; total week’s screen time in hours and minutes; number of days with more than 300 minutes of screen time
  • outputs the average weekly minutes of screen time for the whole class
  • outputs the name of the student with the lowest weekly screen time.
You must use pseudocode or program code and add comments to explain how your code works.
All inputs and outputs must contain suitable messages.
Assume that the array StudentName[] and the variable ClassSize already contain the required data.
You do not need to declare any arrays or variables; you may assume that this has already been done.

ck.lab: 3 students: Ana 25 h 0 min (3 days over 300), Ben 3 h 40 min (0), Cai 28 h 20 min (2); class average 1140; lowest Ben
ck.pre:
CONSTANT ClassSize ← 3
DECLARE StudentName : ARRAY[1:3] OF STRING
DECLARE ScreenTime : ARRAY[1:3, 1:7] OF INTEGER
// test data
StudentName[1] ← "Ana"
StudentName[2] ← "Ben"
StudentName[3] ← "Cai"

pts: R1: inputs each student's daily screen time and calculates their weekly total (input, iteration, totalling)
R2: counts the days with more than 300 minutes and calculates the class's average weekly screen time (selection, counting, iteration, average)

R3: finds the student with the lowest weekly total; outputs each student's name, weekly time in hours and minutes and days over 300, then the class average and the lowest student's name (minimum, output)
g: Marked in levels: AO2 (up to 9 marks) for the programming techniques and data structures used; AO3 (up to 6 marks) for comments, meaningful identifiers, logic and accuracy.
Use the array and variable names given in the scenario exactly.
All inputs and outputs need suitable messages.
ms.code:
ClassTotal ← 0
LowestIndex ← 1
FOR Student ← 1 TO ClassSize
    Total ← 0
    DaysOver300 ← 0
    // input this student's minutes for each of the 7 days
    FOR Day ← 1 TO 7
        OUTPUT StudentName[Student], ", enter your minutes of screen time for day ", Day
        INPUT ScreenTime[Student, Day]
        Total ← Total + ScreenTime[Student, Day]
        IF ScreenTime[Student, Day] > 300
          THEN
            DaysOver300 ← DaysOver300 + 1
        ENDIF
    NEXT Day
    // output this student's results, with the total in hours and minutes
    OUTPUT StudentName[Student]
    OUTPUT "Screen time: ", DIV(Total, 60), " hours ", MOD(Total, 60), " minutes"
    OUTPUT "Days with more than 300 minutes: ", DaysOver300
    ClassTotal ← ClassTotal + Total
    // keep track of the student with the lowest weekly total
    IF Student = 1 OR Total < LowestTotal
      THEN
        LowestTotal ← Total
        LowestIndex ← Student
    ENDIF
NEXT Student
OUTPUT "Average weekly screen time for the class: ", ClassTotal / ClassSize, " minutes"
OUTPUT "Lowest weekly screen time: ", StudentName[LowestIndex]
